newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate dips to 5 percent in August.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate dips to 5 percent in August.

text.p: Florida's unemployment rate dipped to 5 percent in August from 5.2 percent in July and 5.4 percent a year ago, state Labor Secretary Doug Jamerson said Tuesday.

The August figure was unchanged from June, and represents 350,000 unemployed Floridians out of a civilian workforce of 6.99 million. Total nonfarm employment for August was 6.07 million, ain increase of 168,300 jobs or 2.8 percent from August of last year.

Services added the most jobs, 79,700, over the year and had the second fastest growth rate, 3.9 percent. The services growth rate has been declining since October when it reached 7.3 percent. Most of the weakness has been in the business, health, legal, engineering and management groups.

Trade increased by 45,700 jobs or 3 percent over the year. Construction was unchanged in recent months but has increased over the year, with two-thirds of the gains in the special trade contractor industry group.

Manufacturing declined by 2,600 jobs over the year, with all of the decline in nondurable goods. The transportaiton, communications and public utilities sector grew by 8,400 jobs or 2.8 percent over the year while finance, insurance and real estate grew by 8,900 jobs or 2.4 percent. Government increased by 22,000 jobs or 2.6 percent over the year.
All of Florida's metropolitan areas had over the year increases. The Tampa-St. Petersburg area gained the most jobs, 27,700, while Fort Lauderdale had the fastest growth rate, 3.9 percent.

Nearly two-thirds of Florida' 67 counties had unemployment rates below the national average of 5.1 percent in August. Liberty County had the lowest unemployment rate, 2 percent, while Hendry County had the highest, 23.3 percent.
Overall, counties with the highest unemployment rates were in the agricultural areas of central and south Florida, where seasonal increases normally occur in the summer, Jamerson said.
